sentences.text: Shakajlura is an extinct genus documented from a partial skull and assorted fragmentary skeletal pieces.
The species Shakajlura riojanensis was formally named in 2026 by Ariel F. Cardillo and colleagues.
Shakajlura adds a new element to the suite of apex predators known from the Chañares Formation.
Current analyses place Shakajlura as an early-diverging member of Paracrocodylomorpha, a clade that includes the ancestors of crocodylomorphs.
Nevertheless, researchers acknowledge that it might alternatively belong to the early branch of Loricata, the lineage leading to modern crocodiles and their relatives.
It lived during the Ladinian to Carnian intervals of the Triassic period.
The fossils date to between 241.464 and 227.3 million years ago and were recovered from the Tarjadia Assemblage Zone of the Chañares Formation in La Rioja Province, northwestern Argentina.
